annotations.description:
Optional. Annotations on the cluster. This field has the same
restrictions as Kubernetes annotations. The total size of all keys and
values combined is limited to 256k. Key can have 2 segments: prefix (optional)
and name (required), separated by a slash (/). Prefix must be a DNS subdomain.
Name must be 63 characters or less, begin and end with alphanumerics,
with dashes (-), underscores (_), dots (.), and alphanumerics between.


**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the annotations present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_annotations' for all of the annotations present on the resource.
annotations.rationale: Annotations are metadata and do not directly impact security, but improper use could expose sensitive information if secrets or internal details are included.

deletion_policy.description: This field uses a custom implementation please refer to documentation under /hashicorp/terraform-provider-google-beta/website/docs/r/container_attached_cluster.html.markdown for specifics
deletion_policy.rationale: Selects how the attached-cluster registration is torn down (DELETE vs DELETE_IGNORE_ERRORS). This governs control-plane cleanup behavior on destroy; orphaned-metadata/hygiene is an operational concern rather than a confidentiality/integrity/exposure control, so it does not match a security archetype.

description.description:
A human readable description of this attached cluster. Cannot be longer
than 255 UTF-8 encoded bytes.
description.rationale: This field is informational only and does not affect system behavior or access control. However, sensitive information should not be included in descriptions.

distribution.description:
The Kubernetes distribution of the underlying attached cluster. Supported values:
"eks", "aks", "generic". The generic distribution provides the ability to register
or migrate any CNCF conformant cluster.
distribution.rationale: Declares the underlying Kubernetes distribution (eks/aks/generic) of the externally-managed cluster being attached. This is a descriptor of the team's existing cluster, not a security toggle on it; constraining which CNCF-conformant distributions a team may register is overreaching and maps to no archetype.

location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

name.rationale: The name is primarily an identifier and does not influence security unless it exposes sensitive information through naming conventions.

platform_version.description: The platform version for the cluster (e.g. '1.23.0-gke.1').
platform_version.rationale: Using outdated or unsupported platform versions exposes the cluster to known security vulnerabilities and potential integration failures with GCP services. Maintaining a modern platform version ensures that the latest security patches and performance improvements are applied.

project.rationale: Ensures resources are deployed within the intended project boundary for proper governance and access control.

authorization.description: Configuration related to the cluster RBAC settings.

authorization.admin_groups.description:
Groups that can perform operations as a cluster admin. A managed
ClusterRoleBinding will be created to grant the 'cluster-admin' ClusterRole
to the groups. Up to ten admin groups can be provided.

For more info on RBAC, see
https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/rbac/#user-facing-roles
authorization.admin_groups.rationale: Lists groups granted the cluster-admin ClusterRole via a managed RBAC binding. Which groups a team grants admin to is an access-assignment decision we leave to teams (like IAM role/member assignment); a generic policy cannot name approved groups without hardcoding identities, so it is not a policy target.

authorization.admin_users.description:
Users that can perform operations as a cluster admin. A managed
ClusterRoleBinding will be created to grant the 'cluster-admin' ClusterRole
to the users. Up to ten admin users can be provided.

For more info on RBAC, see
https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/rbac/#user-facing-roles
authorization.admin_users.rationale: Lists individual users granted the cluster-admin ClusterRole via a managed RBAC binding. Choosing which users hold admin is a team access-assignment decision; a platform policy cannot enumerate approved users without hardcoding emails, so it is not a generic policy target (we police public/wildcard principals on IAM members instead).

binary_authorization.evaluation_mode.description: Configure Binary Authorization evaluation mode. Possible values: ["DISABLED", "PROJECT_SINGLETON_POLICY_ENFORCE"]
binary_authorization.evaluation_mode.rationale: Sets Binary Authorization evaluation mode (DISABLED vs PROJECT_SINGLETON_POLICY_ENFORCE). Requiring it be enabled enforces image-signature/attestation verification so only trusted images run — a clear enable-security-feature archetype; a generic boolean-style policy requiring enforcement is feasible.

fleet.project.description: The number of the Fleet host project where this cluster will be registered.
fleet.project.rationale: The Fleet host project defines the administrative and governance boundary for the cluster. Assigning the cluster to an incorrect or unauthorized project can lead to improper access controls, policy misalignment, and potential exposure to unauthorized administrators.

logging_config.component_config.description: The configuration of the logging components

logging_config.component_config.enable_c.description: The components to be enabled. Possible values: ["SYSTEM_COMPONENTS", "WORKLOADS"]
logging_config.component_config.enable_c.rationale: Configuring specific logging components ensures that critical system-level data is streamed to Google Cloud Logging for long-term retention and analysis.

monitoring_config.managed_prometheus_con.description: Enable Google Cloud Managed Service for Prometheus in the cluster.

monitoring_config.managed_prometheus_con.rationale: Managed Prometheus provides a scalable, secure way to collect metrics from the cluster. Disabling it creates a blind spot in the infrastructure's security posture.

oidc_config.description:
OIDC discovery information of the target cluster.

Kubernetes Service Account (KSA) tokens are JWT tokens signed by the cluster
API server. This fields indicates how GCP services
validate KSA tokens in order to allow system workloads (such as GKE Connect
and telemetry agents) to authenticate back to GCP.

Both clusters with public and private issuer URLs are supported.
Clusters with public issuers only need to specify the 'issuer_url' field
while clusters with private issuers need to provide both
'issuer_url' and 'jwks'.

oidc_config.issuer_url.description: A JSON Web Token (JWT) issuer URI. 'issuer' must start with 'https://'
oidc_config.issuer_url.rationale: Restricting OIDC issuer URLs to approved identity providers prevents unauthorized authentication into the Kubernetes cluster. Using unapproved providers or non-HTTPS URIs could allow attackers to spoof identities and gain access to cluster resources.

oidc_config.jwks.description: OIDC verification keys in JWKS format (RFC 7517).
oidc_config.jwks.rationale: A valid, Base64-encoded JSON Web Key Set (JWKS) is essential for the cluster to securely validate identity tokens. If the JWKS is missing, empty, or improperly formatted, the cluster cannot verify signatures on incoming JWTs, which breaks the secure authentication chain for system workloads.

proxy_config.kubernetes_secret.description: The Kubernetes Secret resource that contains the HTTP(S) proxy configuration.

proxy_config.kubernetes_secret.name.description: Name of the kubernetes secret containing the proxy config.

proxy_config.kubernetes_secret.namespace.description: Namespace of the kubernetes secret containing the proxy config.
proxy_config.kubernetes_secret.namespace.rationale: Names the Kubernetes namespace holding the proxy-config secret. This is an identifier/reference to where the secret lives; a generic policy cannot pin allowed namespace names without hardcoding them, which is overreaching, and the field does not itself toggle a security control.

security_posture_config.description: Enable/Disable Security Posture API features for the cluster.

security_posture_config.vulnerability_mo.description: Sets the mode of the Kubernetes security posture API's workload vulnerability scanning. Possible values: ["VULNERABILITY_DISABLED", "VULNERABILITY_ENTERPRISE"]
security_posture_config.vulnerability_mo.rationale: Enables continuous vulnerability scanning to detect known security issues in workloads and dependencies.
